_comment: Model registry — the single source of truth for which inference models the
scanner can run under. Read by shared/models.ts (TypeScript stages) and by
run.sh / diff.sh / seed-upstream.sh (bash, via node), so the three can never
drift apart.
Adding a model is a data change, not a code change: append one entry to
`targets`. Nothing under tools/scanner/*/src/ needs to know it exists.
A target's KEY is also its run-artifact namespace: runs/<key>/<stage>/.
Key on the model, not the vendor — api.openai.com serves luna, terra and sol,
and each needs its own isolated run tree to be comparable.
Optional per-target fields beyond the API dialect (see models.ts for the full
schema): `max_concurrency` is a vendor-documented in-flight ceiling the
auto-derived concurrency never exceeds; `benchmark` marks a target MEASURED and
carries its lab result, copied from docs/benchmarking-results.md and pinned to
it by guard.test.ts. A target without `benchmark` is unmeasured, and so is every
entry a user adds through an overlay or the generic endpoint below.
Pricing and planning fields, all optional (a target without them prices and
runs exactly as before): `long_context` {threshold_tokens, input_multiplier,
output_multiplier} applies to a whole request whose prompt passes the threshold;
`service_tiers` {<tier>: {multiplier, label}} lists the tiers the API may report
in `service_tier`, and declaring it is what makes the scanner pin a tier (any
tier string not listed is unpriced and stops the run); `regional_endpoint_pattern`
is a regex on the base URL's host and `regional_uplift` the multiplier when it
matches; `web_search_usd_per_call` prices a web-search tool call; `calibration`
{output_per_input, chars_per_token, seconds_per_call, source} seeds the run
estimate until a reports folder has its own measured runs. See shared/pricing.ts.
`product_default_provider` is the model the product CLI (`npx secscan`) uses when
nothing selects one. `default_provider` stays the lab's default: benchmark runs,
run.sh and every stage launched by hand resolve to it, unchanged.
`generic_openai_compatible` is not a target. It is the template the CLI's
--base-url/--model/--api-key-env flags fill in at runtime (OpenRouter, other
vendors, a local Ollama or LM Studio). The model id, endpoint and credential
variable come from the environment variables it names, never from code.

generic_openai_compatible.label: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint
generic_openai_compatible.notes: Filled in from the environment by models.ts when both model_env and base_url_env are set. api_key_env_env names the variable that in turn names the credential variable, so the key itself never passes through a flag or a config file. The default is a dedicated variable rather than any vendor's: defaulting to OPENAI_API_KEY would send an OpenAI key to whatever third-party endpoint --base-url names. A local server that ignores keys still needs a non-empty value (the SDK refuses an empty one), e.g. SCANNER_CUSTOM_API_KEY=local. price_env takes 'input/output' USD per MTok; without it the target is unpriced and --max-cost refuses to run. max_tokens is the dialect most OpenAI-compatible servers accept (Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter); a server that needs max_completion_tokens belongs in a models.json overlay instead.

luna.label: GPT-5.6 Luna
luna.notes: Long-context (>272K prompt) rates are 0.4/1.8 and are NOT modelled: the registry carries one rate pair, so a long-context run under-reports. GPT-5.x reasoning models reject max_tokens with a 400, and reject any temperature but the default, so steering happens through the prompt and through reasoning_effort. reasoning_effort was added 2026-07-31: runs 1-5 sent none at all and therefore ran at the endpoint's default, so four rounds of playbook work were tuned against the cheapest tier of the family at that tier's own cheapest effort. Re-measured 2026-08-01 on the 40-lane platform against a matched control: high effort alone is recall 53.6% -> 63.9%, 10 entries gained and 0 lost. Paired with Stage 2's default trace loop it is 67.0% recall and 85.6% localization, the shipped arm — see docs/run-history.md 2026-08-01 and docs/architecture/stage2-lane-loop.md. max_output_tokens must move with the effort: reasoning tokens are billed as output AND counted against the cap, and at this effort 42% of calls exceed 8000, where a truncated body is unparseable JSON that Stage 2 records as a lane that found nothing — measured recall 63.9% -> 37.1% at an 8000 cap. Raised 24000 -> 64000 on 2026-08-01. The 14584 figure was the highest completion on run 6's workload only; a deliberately output-maximising lane-shaped probe on the same model returned 29682 completion tokens, so 24000 truncates a harder-but-legitimate lane and the earlier claim that 16000 would do was wrong. 64000 is ~2.2x that measured worst case and half the model's 128000 hard ceiling (established by API rejection, not documentation). The cap is a ceiling, not a spend — billing is per token generated — so headroom is free, while a low cap truncates JSON into what Stage 2 records as a lane that found nothing. All six benchmark targets share 64000 so no cross-model comparison is confounded by differing room to answer. 'medium' is untested. To reproduce runs 1-5 exactly, set SCANNER_REASONING_EFFORT= and SCANNER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000 and HUNT_LOOP=none rather than editing this entry. base_url null means the SDK default, https://api.openai.com/v1. Requires api.openai.com on the environment's egress allowlist.

luna6.label: GPT-6 Luna
luna6.price_tier: standard service tier, short context (prompt <=272K); long context, other tiers and regional endpoints via the fields below

calibration.source: PLACEHOLDER: GPT-5.6 Luna run 6 (2026-08-01) values, not GPT-6 Luna measurements. Replace once GPT-6 Luna has been measured; until then a reports folder's own calibration.json takes precedence over these.

luna6.notes: The product default (product_default_provider); the lab default stays luna. UNMEASURED on the benchmark: no benchmark block, so every surface labels it unmeasured until a scored run is recorded in docs/benchmarking-results.md. Prices are the official rates as of 2026-10-12 from developers.openai.com (model and pricing pages): per MTok input 0.10, cached 0.01, cache write 0.125, output 0.50 at Standard, prompt <=272K. A prompt over 272K bills the WHOLE request at 2x input and cache and 1.5x output (long_context). Tiers: Flex and Batch 0.5x, Priority/Fast 2x — Priority was renamed Fast on 2026-07-30 and which string the API reports in service_tier is unverified, so both are listed; Ultrafast has no published price and is deliberately absent, so a response reporting it is unpriced and stops the run rather than being billed at a guess. Regional (data-residency) hosts such as eu.api.openai.com cost +10%; api.openai.com itself does not match the pattern. Web search is $10 per 1,000 calls. Verified 2026-10-12: cache writes are billed automatically on a prompt's first send (usage reports prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens without any opt-in), so a first call's input is priced at the cache-write rate, not the fresh one; the output cap (max_completion_tokens) does not count toward the tokens-per-minute rate limit at admission, so concurrency is sized on expected rather than capped output; Chat Completions with reasoning_effort high and strict json_schema works. Same endpoint, key and OPENAI_MODEL variable as luna — setting OPENAI_MODEL overrides both targets at once. max_output_tokens 64000 matches luna's for the same reason (reasoning tokens are billed and counted as output); it is not a measured ceiling for this model. calibration holds GPT-5.6 Luna run 6 placeholders, see its source. base_url null means the SDK default, https://api.openai.com/v1.

terra.label: GPT-5.6 Terra
terra.notes: Long-context rates are 4.0/18.0 and are not modelled. Middle tier of the GPT-5.6 family, same endpoint and key as luna. $2.50/$15 per MTok against luna's $1.00/$6.00. Added 2026-07-29 because every run to date has used the family's cheapest tier: docs/'Cybersecurity models pricing research' records luna as 'the smallest step up available' from qwen on cost grounds, so model capability has never been isolated as a variable.

sol.label: GPT-5.6 Sol
sol.notes: Long-context rates are 10.0/45.0 and are not modelled. Top tier of the GPT-5.6 family, same endpoint and key as luna. $5.00/$30 per MTok, ~5x luna on input. Rated 96.7% on OpenAI's internal CTF suite, which they describe as saturated — read it as 'not capability-limited on security reasoning', not as a percentage of anything. See the pricing research doc's caveats before treating that number as a ranking.

luna-fixed.label: GPT-5.6 Luna (post-fix arm)
luna-fixed.notes: Same model and same rates as luna. Same model as luna. A separate key so the run-5 artifacts in runs/luna/ stay untouched while the same model is re-measured with the 2026-07-29 fixes in force. Exists to separate 'the fixes helped' from 'the model tier helped' — without it, a terra-vs-run-5 delta confounds both. Experiment arm: do not merge to main.

qwen.label: Qwen 3.6 Plus
qwen.notes: DashScope's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Accepts only max_tokens. This was the default target before the registry existed; it is kept so the committed runs/qwen/ baseline stays reproducible. Deliberately unpriced: the vendor bills this model's output at two different rates depending on whether the request runs in thinking mode, and the registry carries one rate pair. A single number here would be wrong for one of the two modes, and pricingFor() returning null prints no cost rather than a wrong one.

qwen37.label: Qwen 3.7 Plus
qwen37.notes: The vendor advertises a limited-time 20% discount not applied here, so actual spend runs below projection until it lapses. The >256K tier is 1.2/4.8 and is not modelled. Added 2026-08-01. A separate target from `qwen` rather than a bump of it: `qwen` pins Qwen 3.6 Plus so the committed runs/qwen/ baseline stays reproducible, and reusing the key would silently repoint that baseline's namespace. Verified 2026-08-01 on the endpoint above: plain completion 200, json_schema strict honoured, temperature 0.1 accepted. Shares DASHSCOPE_API_KEY and QWEN_MODEL with `qwen` — setting QWEN_MODEL therefore overrides BOTH targets at once, which would silently collapse a 3.6-vs-3.7 comparison into one model. Leave it unset.

gemini36flash.label: Gemini 3.6 Flash
gemini36flash.price_tier: standard, flat-rate — the vendor publishes no context tier for this model
gemini36flash.notes: Added 2026-08-02. Reached through Google's OpenAI-compatibility layer, same endpoint and credential as gemini31pro, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change. Output price includes thinking tokens. Cache storage ($1.00 per MTok-hour) is not modelled. Shares GEMINI_MODEL with gemini31pro, so setting that env var overrides BOTH targets at once and would collapse a pro-vs-flash comparison into one model — leave it unset. max_output_tokens 64000 matches the other benchmark targets so no model has less room to answer than another; it is not a measured ceiling for this model. Note gemini31pro was observed declining an exhaustive-enumeration task (862 output tokens where peers emitted 25k-31k); whether this model shares that behaviour is unmeasured, and it matters because recall is monotone in trace length.

gemini31pro.label: Gemini 3.1 Pro
gemini31pro.notes: Output price includes thinking tokens. The >200K tier is 4.0/18.0 and is not modelled, so a lane whose prompt crosses 200K under-reports by ~50%. Added 2026-08-01. Reached through Google's OpenAI-compatibility layer, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change; the /v1beta/openai suffix on base_url is what selects that layer. The model id is gemini-3.1-pro-preview — the bare 'gemini-3.1-pro' 404s with NOT_FOUND. Verified 2026-08-01: plain completion 200, json_schema strict honoured. max_output_tokens is set high for the same reason as luna's and matters MORE here: a 16-token probe returned finish_reason 'length' with completion_tokens 0 and an empty body, because thinking consumed the entire budget before any content was emitted. Downstream that is indistinguishable from a lane that found nothing, so do not lower this cap without re-measuring. 24000 is inherited from luna's slack rather than measured on this model — the highest completion actually observed here is unknown.

glm52.label: GLM-5.2
glm52.notes: CONCURRENCY: Z.ai documents a hard in-flight limit of 10 concurrent requests for GLM-5.2 — a per-model cap, distinct from RPM/TPM and exposed in no response header, so it is discoverable only from the vendor's docs. HUNT_CONCURRENCY must be <= 10. The 2026-08-02 benchmark run used 32 before this was known: it completed correctly because the backoff absorbed every 429 and no lane was lost, but 10% of calls were throttled and its ~18.5 min wall clock is therefore not a runtime this model can deliver within its limits (C=10 projects to ~50 min). Recall, tokens and cost are unaffected — a 429 is rejected before generation. EFFORT: reasoning_effort=high is set and the endpoint honours the parameter — reasoning_effort=minimal drives reasoning_tokens to 0, proving it is not ignored — but it is NOT established that high exceeds this endpoint's default: three samples each gave baseline 935/924/652 and high 1042/540/586, fully overlapping. Set for consistency across benchmark targets; do not cite as a measured uplift for this model. Cache storage is free for a limited period and is not modelled. Added 2026-08-01. Z.ai's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change. Credential env var is ZAI_API_KEY, not a GLM_-prefixed name. Verified 2026-08-01: plain completion 200, json_schema strict honoured. A first attempt on 2026-08-01 returned HTTP 429 code 1113 'Insufficient balance' — auth had already succeeded at that point, so read a 1113 as an unfunded account rather than a bad key. The same model is also resold through DashScope at the same list price; this entry uses the vendor endpoint directly.

opus5.label: Claude Opus 5
opus5.price_tier: standard first-party API, global inference_geo, 5m cache writes
opus5.notes: EFFORT: reasoning_effort=high is set per the benchmark mandate. The endpoint ACCEPTS it without error, but no reasoning tokens appeared in the response on a probe where gemini and qwen both reported some — it may be accepted-and-ignored on this compatibility layer. Unresolved; re-check before citing any effort-related result for this target. The batch discount (50%) and the 1.1x us-only inference_geo multiplier are not modelled. Fast mode is 10/50 and is not used. Added 2026-08-01. VERIFIED 2026-08-01 via shared/preflight.ts: model id resolves, plain completion returns content with finish_reason=stop, and json_schema strict is honoured. Reached through Anthropic's OpenAI-compatibility layer at /v1/chat/completions, so it runs the existing SDK client with no code change. The credential var is SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: this runs inside Claude Code, whose harness strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the container (its own sessions authenticate through the account), so that name cannot carry a scanner credential here — it arrives unset no matter where it is configured, and the key had to come in through the environment's setup script. Same reason base_url_env is SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: the ambient ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set without the /v1 suffix and would resolve every call to a 404 path. max_output_tokens 24000 is inherited slack rather than a measured ceiling — no completion length has been observed on this target under a real stage prompt.

sonnet5.label: Claude Sonnet 5
sonnet5.price_tier: standard first-party API, global inference_geo, 5m cache writes, INTRODUCTORY
sonnet5._note_see_also: sonnet5cli is the same model reached through the Claude Code CLI transport. Keep the two entries' prices identical or the two rows stop being comparable on cost.
sonnet5.notes: EFFORT: reasoning_effort=high is set per the benchmark mandate. Accepted without error but no reasoning tokens observed — see opus5, same compatibility layer, same open question. INTRODUCTORY pricing, expires 2026-08-31. From 2026-09-01 the rate becomes 3.0/15.0 (cached 0.30, 5m write 3.75), a 50% increase that takes a full run from ~$43.88 to ~$65.83. Update this entry on that date or every later run under-reports by a third. Added 2026-08-01. VERIFIED 2026-08-01 via shared/preflight.ts: model id resolves, plain completion returns content with finish_reason=stop, and json_schema strict is honoured. Same transport and same credential handling as opus5 — see that entry for why the vars are SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SCANNER_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Shares ANTHROPIC_MODEL with opus5, so setting that env var overrides both targets at once and would collapse an opus-vs-sonnet comparison into a single model. Leave it unset. max_output_tokens 24000 is inherited slack rather than a measured ceiling.

sonnet5cli.label: Claude Sonnet 5 (Claude Code CLI transport)
sonnet5cli.price_tier: standard first-party API, global inference_geo, 5m cache writes, INTRODUCTORY
sonnet5cli.notes: Claude Sonnet 5 measured through the local Claude Code binary in headless mode (`claude -p`) rather than over HTTP, so the run draws on a Max subscription instead of a metered key. Same weights and same model id as `sonnet5`; a SEPARATE key because the transport is not neutral and the two must never share a results row. Added 2026-08-02. TRANSPORT DELTAS, all measured on 2026-08-02 and all of which must travel with any number from this target: (1) ~170 tokens per call of irreducible CLI framing survive `--system-prompt ''` (175 input tokens on a 5-token prompt), about 184k tokens across a 1,082-call run; (2) structured output is a forced tool call via `--json-schema`, not `response_format: json_schema strict`; (3) `--effort high` is Claude Code's thinking budget and IS applied, whereas `sonnet5`'s `reasoning_effort` over the OpenAI-compat layer is accepted with no reasoning tokens ever observed — since recall is monotone in trace length this biases THIS target upward, and a sonnet5cli-vs-sonnet5 gap is not a capability result; (4) the trace loop's second turn is a `--resume`, which the CLI serves partly from prompt cache, so input bills cheaper here than the uncached compat path. SANDBOX: the transport passes `--tools "" --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands` on EVERY invocation including resumes. Measured: a session resumed WITHOUT re-passing `--tools ""` regains the full tool set and will read an arbitrary file off disk — which for this project means the answer key one directory above the corpus. guard.test.ts asserts both paths. COST: computed downstream from the CLI's reported per-model token counts against the rates above. Do NOT use the CLI's own costUSD field — it prices this model at 3.0/15.0, the post-2026-08-31 rate, and disagrees with this entry. The rates here are the August 2026 introductory rates and are the ones this benchmark reports. api_key_env and model_env are placeholders that are deliberately never read: this transport authenticates through the CLI's own session and takes its model id from `model`. base_url is null for the same reason — there is no HTTP endpoint.
